# Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17  
## Acute Hemorrhagic Respiratory Failure Syndrome

> *This article describes a fictional pathogen and fictional disease for creative writing, gaming, or visual-world-building purposes. It is not a real virus, diagnosis, or medical condition.*

**Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17**, informally known as **A17**, is a fictional respiratory virus associated with **Acute Hemorrhagic Respiratory Failure Syndrome** (**AHRFS**). In the fictional setting, A17 causes a fast-progressing illness marked by fever, coughing, chest pain, difficulty breathing, and bleeding involving the upper airways in severe cases.

It was first identified during the fictional **Veyra Respiratory Crisis**, an outbreak centered in the Old Harbor district of the city of Veyra. Its dramatic late-stage symptoms led some media outlets to call it the **“Crimson Lung Virus.”**

## Classification

| Category | Information |
|---|---|
| Scientific designation | *Orthomyxoviridae* Strain A17 |
| Common name | A17 |
| Associated syndrome | Acute Hemorrhagic Respiratory Failure Syndrome |
| Abbreviation | AHRFS |
| Type | Fictional respiratory virus |
| Family | *Orthomyxoviridae* |
| Primary system affected | Respiratory system |
| Fictional origin | Old Harbor District, Veyra |
| First reported | October 17, 20██ |
| Status | Contained; sporadic fictional outbreaks reported |

## Acute Hemorrhagic Respiratory Failure Syndrome

**Acute Hemorrhagic Respiratory Failure Syndrome**, abbreviated **AHRFS**, is the fictional disease syndrome caused by Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17. It is characterized by rapid inflammation of the airways and lungs, which can lead to impaired oxygen exchange and respiratory failure.

In severe fictional cases, damage to small blood vessels in the respiratory tract causes bleeding, producing blood-streaked mucus, nosebleeds, or bleeding from the mouth following intense coughing episodes. The syndrome’s name comes from its combination of sudden onset, respiratory distress, and hemorrhagic symptoms.

## Signs and symptoms

A17 infection is typically portrayed as developing over several stages.

| Stage | Typical fictional symptoms |
|---|---|
| Early stage | Fever, chills, headache, fatigue, sore throat, dry cough |
| Progressive stage | Persistent cough, chest pressure, dizziness, hoarseness, shortness of breath |
| Severe stage | Blood-streaked mucus, nosebleeds, severe chest pain, confusion, low oxygen levels |
| Critical stage | Hemorrhagic airway damage, respiratory failure, shock, and loss of consciousness |

Not every fictional patient develops bleeding. In story settings, these symptoms are generally depicted as a sign that the infection has entered a critical stage.

## Transmission

In fictional reports, A17 spreads through respiratory droplets and close contact with infected people. Transmission is often associated with enclosed, poorly ventilated settings such as schools, shelters, hospitals, transit stations, and residential towers.

Fictional authorities recommend the following during outbreaks:

- Use protective masks in designated containment zones.
- Stay home after developing fever, coughing, or breathing difficulty.
- Avoid crowded indoor locations.
- Improve airflow in homes, classrooms, and workplaces.
- Seek emergency care for unexplained bleeding or severe breathing problems.

## Discovery

The first confirmed fictional case was recorded on October 17, 20██, at **St. Elian Medical Center** in Veyra. The patient, an Old Harbor dockworker, was admitted with high fever, chest pain, and a violent cough that later became blood-streaked.

At first, officials suspected chemical exposure from shipping facilities near the harbor. After additional patients appeared among coworkers and nearby residents, a laboratory team detected an unidentified influenza-like viral agent. It received the temporary classification **Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17**, referring to the date connected with the earliest confirmed case record.

## Veyra Respiratory Crisis

The first large-scale fictional outbreak of A17 became known as the **Veyra Respiratory Crisis**. It began in the Old Harbor district and expanded into East Veyra, especially the densely populated **District 9**.

Measures enacted during the crisis included:

- Emergency school and business closures.
- Curfews in affected neighborhoods.
- Transit-station screening checkpoints.
- Mandatory masks in public indoor spaces.
- Conversion of sports arenas into temporary treatment centers.
- Quarantine of several residential buildings.

The outbreak’s public image was shaped by footage of emergency workers in protective equipment, sealed hospital wings, abandoned train platforms, and red warning notices posted across the city.

## Treatment

There is no definitive cure for A17 in most versions of the fictional setting. Care focuses on supporting breathing, preventing complications, and isolating infected individuals.

Common fictional treatments include:

- Supplemental oxygen.
- Respiratory monitoring.
- Fever and pain management.
- Intravenous fluids.
- Intensive-care ventilation for critical cases.
- The experimental antiviral **Virelax-17**.

Virelax-17 is often portrayed as controversial: it may reduce the speed of disease progression when administered early, but supplies are limited and side effects are severe. This can create a strong plot conflict involving hospital staff, government agencies, private laboratories, and civilians.

## Public response and conspiracy theories

Because the severe form of AHRFS involves visible bleeding, fear spread faster than reliable information during the Veyra outbreak. The phrase **“A cough is not always a cold”** appeared on public warning posters and emergency broadcasts.

Several fictional theories emerged:

- A17 escaped from a restricted biomedical laboratory.
- The virus arrived aboard an unregistered cargo ship.
- Authorities concealed early cases to protect Veyra’s port economy.
- The outbreak was connected to contaminated ventilation systems beneath Old Harbor.
- Virelax-17 existed before the first reported case, suggesting prior knowledge of the virus.

No explanation has been officially confirmed within the fictional universe.

## See also

- Veyra Respiratory Crisis  
- St. Elian Medical Center  
- Virelax-17  
- District 9 Quarantine  
- List of fictional viral outbreaks

===== Fictional Orthomyxoviridae Virus ===== {{Short description|Fictional respiratory virus}}
''This article is about a fictional pathogen created for a creative project. '''Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17''' and '''acute hemorrhagic respiratory failure syndrome''' are not real medical entities.''
'''Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17''' ('''A17'''), associated with the disease '''acute hemorrhagic respiratory failure syndrome''' ('''AHRFS'''), is a '''respiratory virus''' described in the setting as a highly lethal pathogen affecting the lungs and airways. It is associated with fever, severe coughing, respiratory distress, airway bleeding, acute respiratory failure, and death in advanced cases. In the setting, no approved cure, vaccine, or reliably effective antiviral treatment exists for A17 infection. Medical personnel can provide only supportive care, such as oxygen support, ventilation, fluids, blood-pressure support, and isolation precautions. The absence of a definitive treatment, combined with rapid transmission in enclosed spaces, makes A17 the central cause of the '''Spanish Respiratory Crisis'''. A17 was first identified in the city of [[Barcelona]] after a cluster of nurses from the Old Harbor district were admitted to [[Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron]] with unexplained fever, chest pain, and rapidly progressing respiratory failure. The virus later received the public nickname '''Bleeding Heart''' because of reports of severe coughing accompanied by blood-streaked mucus and bleeding from the upper airways. == Classification and naming == {| class="wikitable" |- ! Classification ! Designation |- | Family | ''Orthomyxoviridae'' |- | Strain name | A17 |- | Associated disease | Acute hemorrhagic respiratory failure syndrome |- | Abbreviation | AHRFS |- | Common names | A17, Crimson Lung, Red Cough, Harbor Fever |- | Type | Enveloped respiratory RNA virus |- | Primary system affected | Respiratory system |- | First documented outbreak | Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron |- | First documented case | 17 October 2018 |- | Status | Global Outbreak |} The name '''A17''' originated from the internal laboratory designation applied to the earliest verified respiratory sample. According to medical records, the letter “A” referred to an unidentified influenza-like viral grouping, while “17” referred to the date on which the first sample was processed. The disease caused by A17 infection is called '''acute hemorrhagic respiratory failure syndrome'''. The term ''acute'' refers to the rapid progression of the illness, while ''hemorrhagic'' refers to bleeding caused by damage to respiratory tissue and blood vessels. ''Respiratory failure'' refers to the loss of the lungs’ ability to supply sufficient oxygen to the body. == Virology == In the setting, A17 is described as an enveloped RNA virus with a strong affinity for cells lining the throat, bronchi, and lungs. Following exposure, the virus enters the respiratory tract and replicates inside airway cells. The illness is portrayed as being caused by both viral replication and an extreme inflammatory response. In severe cases, inflammation damages the small air sacs of the lungs and nearby blood vessels. Fluid, inflammatory material, and blood may then enter the airways, making oxygen exchange difficult or impossible. Laboratory documents describe A17 as relatively unstable on open surfaces but particularly dangerous in poorly ventilated indoor settings. Schools, apartment buildings, public transportation systems, medical waiting rooms, shelters, and workplaces are frequently identified as major transmission locations. == Transmission == A17 is primarily depicted as spreading through airborne respiratory particles released during coughing, sneezing, speaking, singing, or prolonged close contact. Transmission is considered most likely in crowded and poorly ventilated indoor environments. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Route of transmission ! Significance |- | Airborne respiratory particles | Considered the principal route of spread, especially indoors |- | Close face-to-face contact | High risk during caregiving, conversation, transport, or household exposure |- | Contaminated hands and surfaces | Considered a secondary route if contaminated hands touch the eyes, nose, or mouth |- | Medical exposure | A major risk for unprotected health-care workers |- | Blood contact | Possible in severe cases, but not considered the primary route of infection |} One of the major concerns surrounding A17 is '''presymptomatic transmission'''. Infected individuals may spread the virus before they recognize that they are ill. Because early symptoms can resemble a common respiratory infection, outbreaks may grow before hospitals or authorities recognize a pattern. == Signs and symptoms == The incubation period for A17 is generally described as lasting between two and seven days. The illness often begins with symptoms resembling influenza or a severe cold, including fever, exhaustion, sore throat, body aches, and a dry cough. Symptoms may worsen quickly after the onset of breathing difficulty. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Clinical stage ! Typical duration ! Reported features |- | Incubation | 2–7 days | No visible symptoms; possible transmission to others |- | Initial illness | 1–3 days | Fever, chills, fatigue, headache, sore throat, dry cough |- | Pulmonary progression | 1–2 days | Chest pressure, worsening cough, dizziness, wheezing, shortness of breath, pale skin, bleeding airways |- | Hemorrhagic phase | Several hours to 2 days | Blood-streaked mucus, nosebleeds, bleeding after coughing, low oxygen levels, gray skin, blood tears, internal bleeding |- | Critical failure | Variable | Severe oxygen deprivation, shock, unconsciousness, multi-organ dysfunction, death |} Bleeding is not present in all A17 infections. However, blood in mucus, severe nosebleeds, or bleeding from the mouth after coughing are treated as signs of advanced respiratory damage. Emergency notices issued during the French outbreak instructed residents to seek immediate help for severe chest pain, confusion, fainting, blue or gray lips, rapid breathing, or coughing up blood. == Acute hemorrhagic respiratory failure syndrome == '''Acute hemorrhagic respiratory failure syndrome''' ('''AHRFS''') is the severe disease state associated with Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17 infection. It occurs when extensive inflammation and blood-vessel damage prevent the lungs from moving enough oxygen into the bloodstream. In clinical reports, patients with AHRFS may deteriorate over hours rather than days. Severe inflammation may fill the lungs with fluid and blood, while declining oxygen levels place strain on the heart, brain, kidneys, and other organs. Patients can become confused, lose consciousness, or enter shock before respiratory collapse. AHRFS is particularly feared because it may develop in people who initially appear to have only mild symptoms. The sudden transition from ordinary fever and coughing to life-threatening breathing failure is a recurring element of the Spanish outbreak narrative. == Mortality and prognosis == A17 is portrayed as a highly lethal disease. Reported mortality figures vary because many deaths occur outside formal medical settings, testing supplies are limited, and hospitals may become overwhelmed during large outbreaks. During the Spain Respiratory Crisis, the Spanish Ministry of Health initially reported a confirmed-case fatality rate of 12%. Independent medical workers and leaked hospital documents later suggested that the actual rate may have been closer to 20% in districts where oxygen, testing, and intensive-care treatment were unavailable. Among patients admitted with severe respiratory bleeding and AHRFS, mortality was reported to exceed 50%. Groups considered especially vulnerable within the setting include: * Older adults. * Infants and young children. * People with chronic lung disease. * People with heart disease. * People with weakened immune systems. * Pregnant patients. * Residents of crowded housing with poor ventilation. * Health-care workers exposed to repeated high concentrations of the virus. However, public concern is heightened by reports that otherwise healthy teenagers and adults can also experience rapid deterioration. == Diagnosis == Clinicians diagnose suspected A17 infection using a combination of symptom history, known exposure, oxygen measurements, lung imaging, and laboratory analysis of respiratory samples. During the Spanish outbreak, the earliest available test was an experimental molecular assay developed by the [[Centro Nacional de Microbiología,]]. Because testing capacity was limited, hospitals frequently categorized patients as either “confirmed A17,” “probable A17,” or “respiratory illness under investigation.” Reported diagnostic findings include: * Low blood-oxygen levels. * Severe inflammation visible on chest imaging. * Fluid accumulation within the lungs. * Areas of bleeding and damaged lung tissue. * Rapid decline in respiratory capacity. * Detection of A17 genetic material in respiratory samples. Testing delays became politically controversial during the outbreak. Residents of poorer areas, particularly Catalonia and A17-AHRFS nurse housing, reportedly waited longer for testing and hospital admission than residents of wealthier districts. == Prevention and containment == Because no cure, vaccine, or proven antiviral medication is available in the setting, prevention and containment are the primary methods used to limit A17 transmission. Measures adopted by authorities include: * Isolation of people with symptoms. * Protective masks in indoor public areas. * Closure of schools, stadiums, cinemas, and nonessential workplaces. * Emergency ventilation standards for public buildings. * Quarantine orders for households and apartment complexes. * Health screening at transit hubs and district checkpoints. * Contact tracing following confirmed cases. * Temporary medical centers for mild and moderate cases. * Restricted entry to hospitals, morgues, and containment zones. The Spanish government’s policies were heavily criticized. Officials argued that curfews, travel restrictions, and building lockdowns were necessary to prevent the collapse of the health-care system. Civil-rights groups claimed that the restrictions were enforced most aggressively in low-income districts and that residents in those areas received less medical support. == Treatment == There is no cure for Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17 in the setting. No vaccine has been developed, and no antiviral drug has been demonstrated to reliably stop the progression of AHRFS. Medical treatment is limited to supportive care. Depending on severity, hospitals may provide oxygen, mechanical ventilation, intravenous fluids, medication to maintain blood pressure, pain management, fever reduction, blood-product replacement, and intensive monitoring. These measures can stabilize some patients but do not eliminate the virus. Once severe respiratory bleeding and oxygen failure develop, survival is uncertain even in well-equipped hospitals. During the [[La cuarentena en España]], shortages of oxygen, ventilators, protective equipment, intensive-care beds, and trained medical personnel contributed to rising death rates. Some hospitals reportedly enacted emergency triage systems, prioritizing patients judged most likely to survive with limited resources. The experimental drug [[Virelax-17]] was initially promoted as a potential breakthrough. Later reports concluded that it was ineffective against advanced A17 infection. The controversy surrounding its development and distribution became a major source of public anger toward government agencies and pharmaceutical contractors. == Origin theories == The origin of A17 remains unknown within the universe. Official investigations have not established a definitive source of the virus, leading to widespread public speculation and conspiracy theories. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Theory ! Description |- | Zoonotic spillover | A17 crossed from an unidentified animal population to humans near Catalonia Harbor |- | Maritime introduction | The virus arrived aboard an unregistered cargo vessel before spreading among dockworkers |- | Laboratory accident | A17 escaped from a research facility conducting influenza-related experiments |- | Industrial contamination | Toxic environmental exposure weakened residents’ lungs and contributed to the severity of the outbreak |- | Deliberate release | The outbreak was intentionally initiated for political, military, or corporate purposes |} Official accounts favor the zoonotic-spillover theory. Critics dispute this conclusion because of missing port records, gaps in early hospital data, and the unexplained disappearance of surveillance footage from the Old Harbor district. == La cuarentena en España == The '''La cuarentena en España''' was the first recognized major outbreak of Orthomyxoviridae Strain A17. It began in the New Harbor district after several dockworkers were hospitalized with fever, chest pain, persistent coughing, and rapidly worsening respiratory distress. The first documented patient was admitted to Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron on 17 October 2018. By the end of the following week, dozens of similar cases had been reported among dockworkers, their families, transit employees, and residents of nearby apartment buildings. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Date ! Event |- | 17 October 2018 | First officially documented patient admitted to Universitari Vall d’Hebron |- | 20 October 2018 | Three additional dockworkers develop severe respiratory symptoms |- | 23 October 2018 | First recorded death attributed to unexplained hemorrhagic lung failure |- | 27 October 2018 | Schools and markets in New Harbor close temporarily |- | 1 November 2018 | The A17 designation appears in leaked laboratory documents |- | 5 November 2018 | A citywide indoor-mask order is introduced |- | 12 November 2018 | Spain is placed under emergency quarantine |- | 19 November 2018 | Hospitals report shortages of oxygen and intensive-care beds |- | 2 December 2018 | National government deploys military medical units to Spain |- | 14 December 2018 | Authorities state that transmission has slowed, although unofficial deaths continue to rise |} At the height of the crisis, public transportation was halted, sports arenas became overflow medical wards, and entire streets were closed by temporary containment barriers. Red-and-black warning notices, emergency radio broadcasts, and masked medical workers became defining visual symbols of the outbreak. == Social and political impact == The A17 outbreak disrupted daily life throughout the country. Schools moved to emergency remote instruction, businesses closed, supply chains became unstable, and residents faced long lines for food, medication, and protective equipment. The crisis also created intense mistrust of public officials. Many residents believed authorities delayed public warnings to protect Spain’s shipping economy and avoid financial panic. Government officials maintained that early information was incomplete and that releasing it too quickly could have caused disorder. The phrase '''“A cough is not always a cold”''' became the central public-health slogan of the crisis. It appeared on transit advertisements, pharmacy windows, emergency broadcasts, school notices, and social-media warnings. In later accounts, the phrase became associated both with disease awareness and with anger over the delayed response. == In popular culture == Within the setting, A17 and the La cuarentena en España have inspired survivor memoirs, underground radio programs, conspiracy documentaries, horror films, and video games. Common imagery associated with the outbreak includes: * Empty subway platforms. * Sealed hospital corridors. * Emergency alert tones. * Red-stained surgical masks. * Quarantine tape around residential towers. * Flickering warning screens in public transit stations. * Government posters instructing citizens to report symptoms. * Abandoned streets illuminated by emergency vehicles. The outbreak is frequently used to explore themes of government secrecy, public panic, medical inequality, surveillance, isolation, and the consequences of delayed crisis communication. == See also == * [[Acute hemorrhagic respiratory failure syndrome]] * [[La cuarentena en España]] * [[Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron]] * [[Global Health Orginaztion]] * [[Centro Nacional de Microbiología]] * [[Virelax-17]] * [[List of epidemics]] [[Category:Fictional viruses]] [[Category:Fictional diseases]] [[Category:Fictional epidemics]] [[Category:Horror fiction]]

'''Accommodation'''

Accommodation is defined as something that satisfies an individual's needs. When you accommodate someone or offer accommodations, you are offering assistance by fulfilling needs and desires for another individual. Accommodation is derived from the Latin root verb, accommodare, which means to make fit or to adjust. Accommodation was present in Middle French before entering the English language in the late 1500s. During this time, the term was used to describe favors. It was around this time as well that the term was used when referring to temporary housing. In relation to disability, accommodations can range from assisting educational needs, which may include extra time on tests or having access to a sign language interpreter, to physical needs, such as chair lifts in homes or portable ramps to get into buildings. While to many, accommodations are an inclusive fix by allowing individuals with disabilities to participate in everyday life, those with disabilities view accommodations as an inconvenience.  

To many in the disabled individuals, the term accommodation has a negative connotation. The term alludes to the fact that things were built or designed without the thought of including the disabled community. Accommodations act as if accessibility was an afterthought in the construction of an activity, location, or idea. It makes it so that a disabled individual must go through extra steps just to carry out their everyday tasks when ideally, the idea should've been adapted with disabilities in mind in the first place (Accessibility @ UW-Madison). While in a perfect world everyone's needs would be met, it is difficult to make this happen. What works for one person may cause an inconvenience to another, and for individuals who have more unique needs, they might not be represented in society. For these individuals who must continue to ask for accommodations, it is common to feel like an inconvenience, or like special treatment is being received. Asking for accommodations gives power to others, as in order to have an accommodation, disabled individuals must ask someone with an authority position to provide one. After explaining and proving why an accommodation is necessary, those in power decide whether to provide it or not. If they decide against it, the individual is left without the accessibility to society their rights are meant to provide (DisabilityWisdom). The existence of accommodations, while helpful, are a constant reminder of how inaccessible society is. 

 

While this is a reality for many disabled individuals, over the course of time, what used to be known as accommodations are now the norm in many societies. With the help of laws such as the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, main roads have crosswalks with voice features, buildings are built with ramp entrances, and offices have dedicated quiet rooms. Society has evolved by turning what used to be "special" and "inconvenient" requests into normal expectations in society. The increased accessibility in society over the years is a great accomplishment, but it is important to remember how many individuals still deal with the inconveniences of society.

Titan manifestations | notes = }} '''The Battle of Heaven and Earth''' ({{lang-ja|天と地の戦い|Ten to Chi no Tatakai}}) was the final major battle of the [[Attack on Titan]] series. It was fought in 854 between the [[Alliance (Attack on Titan)|Alliance]], a coalition consisting primarily of surviving members of the [[Scout Regiment]] and the Marleyan [[Warrior Unit]], and [[Eren Yeager]] and the forces of the [[Founding Titan]]. The battle began after the Alliance arrived at [[Fort Salta]] in [[Marley]] in an attempt to stop Eren's [[Rumbling]]. Eren had used the power of the Founding Titan to command the Wall Titans to march across the world, destroying much of humanity outside [[Paradis Island]]. The Alliance fought its way onto Eren's Founding Titan while attempting to stop the Rumbling. After a prolonged battle against the Founding Titan's Titan manifestations and the Wall Titans, [[Armin Arlert]] confronted Eren in the Paths while the other members of the Alliance continued fighting on the Founding Titan's body. The battle ultimately ended when [[Mikasa Ackerman]] killed Eren by severing his head from the Founding Titan. Eren's death caused the Rumbling to cease and brought about the disappearance of the power of the Titans. == Background == === The Rumbling === Following the [[Battle of Shiganshina District]] and the deaths of [[Zeke Yeager]] and [[Eren Yeager]]'s allies, Eren gained access to the full power of the [[Founding Titan]]. Eren subsequently initiated the [[Rumbling]], causing the Wall Titans within the Walls of Paradis to begin marching across the world. Eren's objective was to destroy the majority of humanity outside Paradis in order to prevent the island from being destroyed by foreign powers. The Rumbling devastated large areas of the world and killed a vast number of people. The surviving members of the Scout Regiment and the Marleyan Warriors eventually formed an alliance in order to stop Eren. === Formation of the Alliance === The [[Alliance (Attack on Titan)|Alliance]] consisted of former enemies who had previously fought against one another during the conflict between Paradis and Marley. Among its members were [[Armin Arlert]], [[Mikasa Ackerman]], [[Levi Ackerman]], [[Jean Kirstein]], [[Connie Springer]], [[Reiner Braun]], [[Pieck Finger]], and [[Annie Leonhart]]. The group initially traveled by sea and air in pursuit of Eren's advancing Founding Titan. After the death of [[Hange Zoë]], [[Armin Arlert]] assumed command of the Scouts. The Alliance ultimately arrived at [[Fort Salta]], where Marleyan forces and civilians had gathered while attempting to escape the Rumbling. == Forces == === Alliance === The Alliance's forces consisted of the surviving members of the Scout Regiment and former Marleyan Warriors. {| class="wikitable" ! Member ! Role | ! Outcome | | ------------------------------- | | [[Armin Arlert]] | | Colossus Titan; field commander | | Survived | | - | | [[Mikasa Ackerman]] | | Soldier; Ackerman | | Survived | | - | | [[Levi Ackerman]] | | Soldier; Ackerman | | Survived | | - | | [[Jean Kirstein]] | | Soldier | | Survived | | - | | [[Connie Springer]] | | Soldier | | Survived | | - | | [[Reiner Braun]] | | Armored Titan | | Survived | | - | | [[Pieck Finger]] | | Cart Titan | | Survived | | - | | [[Annie Leonhart]] | | Female Titan | | Survived | | - | | [[Falco Grice]] | | Jaw Titan | | Survived | | - | | [[Hange Zoë]] | | Scout commander | | Killed before the battle | | } | === Eren's forces === Eren's forces consisted primarily of the Wall Titans under the control of the Founding Titan. Eren also used the Founding Titan's abilities to create or summon manifestations of previous Titan shifters. The Founding Titan possessed an enormous skeletal body and was connected to the Paths, allowing Eren to exert control over the Titans. == Battle == === Arrival at Fort Salta === The Alliance arrived at Fort Salta aboard an aircraft while the Rumbling approached the area. They intended to reach Eren's Founding Titan and sever his connection to the Founding Titan before the Rumbling could continue. The Alliance initially attempted to communicate with Eren but received no indication that he intended to stop the Rumbling. The group subsequently launched an attack against Eren's Founding Titan. === Assault on the Founding Titan === The Alliance landed on the Founding Titan and immediately came under attack from Titan manifestations created through the Founding Titan's power. The surviving members of the Alliance divided their efforts between defending themselves, locating Eren, and attempting to determine how the Rumbling could be stopped. [[Reiner Braun]] transformed into the Armored Titan and fought the Titan manifestations on the Founding Titan's body. [[Pieck Finger]] used the Cart Titan to transport members of the Alliance across the battlefield. The Alliance suffered significant losses during the fighting. === Battle against the Titan manifestations === The Founding Titan produced manifestations resembling several previous Titan shifters. These Titans attacked the Alliance and prevented the group from reaching Eren. The battle became increasingly difficult as the Alliance was forced to fight numerous Titans while the Wall Titans continued advancing below them. The situation changed when [[Armin Arlert]] was captured and separated from the rest of the Alliance. === Armin and Zeke === Armin was transported into the [[Paths]], where he encountered [[Zeke Yeager]]. Zeke had become disillusioned with his previous ideology and began discussing the meaning of life with Armin. Armin argued that the value of life could be found in ordinary experiences and personal connections rather than in reproduction or grand historical purposes. Zeke eventually helped Armin regain the ability to influence events in the physical world. Other deceased Titan shifters appeared within the Paths and assisted the Alliance by providing their Titans. Their intervention allowed the surviving members of the Alliance to continue fighting the Founding Titan's forces. === Levi and Zeke === [[Levi Ackerman]] remained focused on his promise to kill Zeke. Zeke eventually emerged from the Founding Titan and allowed himself to be killed by Levi. Levi severed Zeke's head, fulfilling the promise he had made to [[Erwin Smith]] and the other fallen members of the Scout Regiment. Zeke's death weakened Eren's connection to the Rumbling. === The Rumbling is stopped === After Zeke's death, the Rumbling temporarily ceased. However, Eren continued to fight and transformed again after his connection to the Founding Titan was disrupted. The Alliance therefore continued its attempt to kill Eren. The battlefield shifted from the Founding Titan to the surrounding area near Fort Salta. === Eren's final transformation === Eren manifested the [[Colossus Titan]] and engaged the Alliance in another confrontation. Armin transformed into the Colossus Titan and fought Eren directly. The two Titans engaged in a massive battle while the remaining members of the Alliance attempted to locate Eren's human body. === Mikasa kills Eren === After discovering Eren's location, the Alliance determined that killing him was necessary to end the conflict permanently. [[Mikasa Ackerman]] entered the Founding Titan and reached Eren's human body. Despite her feelings for Eren, Mikasa chose to kill him. She severed Eren's head from his body and kissed him after his death. Eren's death brought the final confrontation to an end. == Aftermath == The death of Eren ended the [[Rumbling]]. The power of the Titans subsequently disappeared. Subjects of Ymir were no longer capable of transforming into Titans, and the Titan powers possessed by the remaining shifters were eliminated. The surviving members of the Alliance returned to the mainland. The battle marked the effective end of the conflict between Eren and the rest of the world, although the political consequences of the Rumbling continued after the battle. === Death of the Titans === Following Eren's death, the Titan powers disappeared. The surviving Titan shifters were transformed back into humans, ending the nearly two-thousand-year history of the Titan curse. This also ended the existence of the Nine Titans. == Casualties == === Alliance === The Alliance suffered several casualties during the final stages of the Rumbling and the Battle of Heaven and Earth. [[Hange Zoë]] had died shortly before the battle while delaying the Wall Titans to allow the Alliance's aircraft to launch. Several soldiers and former Warriors were killed during the battle itself. Despite the losses, most of the principal members of the Alliance survived. === Eren's forces === Eren was killed by Mikasa. The Wall Titans ceased functioning after the Rumbling was stopped, while the Titan manifestations created by the Founding Titan disappeared following the loss of the Titan power. == Significance == The Battle of Heaven and Earth represents the conclusion of the primary conflict of ''[[Attack on Titan]]''. The battle brought together characters who had previously been enemies, including Eldians from Paradis and Marleyan Warriors. Their cooperation was motivated by the shared objective of stopping Eren and the Rumbling. The battle also ended the Titan era. With the disappearance of the Titan powers, the central supernatural force that had shaped the history of Eldia and Marley for centuries ceased to exist. However, the battle did not permanently eliminate human conflict. The later history of Paradis demonstrated that political and military conflict continued after the end of the Titan era. == Characters involved == {| class="wikitable" ! Character ! Affiliation | ! Status | | ------------------------ | | [[Eren Yeager]] | | Paradis / Founding Titan | | '''Killed''' | | - | | [[Armin Arlert]] | | Alliance | | Survived | | - | | [[Mikasa Ackerman]] | | Alliance | | Survived | | - | | [[Levi Ackerman]] | | Alliance | | Survived | | - | | [[Reiner Braun]] | | Alliance / Marley | | Survived | | - | | [[Pieck Finger]] | | Alliance / Marley | | Survived | | - | | [[Jean Kirstein]] | | Alliance | | Survived | | - | | [[Connie Springer]] | | Alliance | | Survived | | - | | [[Annie Leonhart]] | | Alliance / Marley | | Survived | | - | | [[Falco Grice]] | | Alliance / Marley | | Survived | | - | | [[Hange Zoë]] | | Scout Regiment | | '''Killed''' | | - | | [[Zeke Yeager]] | | Former Marleyan Warrior | | '''Killed''' | | } | == In popular culture == The Battle of Heaven and Earth serves as the climax of the ''Attack on Titan'' manga and anime. It encompasses the final confrontation between Eren and the characters who oppose his decision to initiate the Rumbling. The battle was adapted into the final installments of the ''Attack on Titan'' anime series. == See also == * [[Attack on Titan]] * [[War for Paradis]] * [[Rumbling]] * [[Founding Titan]] * [[Eren Yeager]] * [[Mikasa Ackerman]] * [[Armin Arlert]] * [[Alliance (Attack on Titan)]] == References == {{Reflist}} == Navigation == {{Attack on Titan}} [[Category:Attack on Titan]] [[Category:Fictional battles]] [[Category:Battles in Attack on Titan]] [[Category:854]] [[Category:Marley]]

<text bytes="8887" sha1="j0mlqjweswx3dthhh2lwy4byav4blxf" xml:space="preserve">{{Construction}} Torn's '''Forums''' is a location of both public and private discussion under several categories: * Announcements * My Forums * Main Forums (Torn-Related) * Non-Related Forums (Non Torn-Related) Torn's forums can be found [https://www.torn.com/forums.php here]. ==Rules and Guidelines== To protect users, there are social guidelines that must be adhered to avoid an excessively toxic environment. Please see the current [https://www.torn.com/rules.php rules] under '''Social Violations'''. ==Functions== * Players can post text, tables, hosted images, and hosted videos (using the built-in forum editor). * Forum posts are editable (only the time of last edit will be seen at the end of the post) by author and staff. * Players can accumulate [[Forum#Karma|Karma]] through upvotes for their threads or posts. Downvotes can give negative karma. A player's karma cannot go below zero. ==Categories== ===Announcements=== This is the category where Admins post updates to the game, a weekly patch list that highlights developers current focus, downtime notifications, and applications for staff and the player committee. This allows players to stay informed about the recent happenings in Torn. Players cannot post in this section. ===My Forums=== These are player specific forums which may change from time to time depending on the status of the player. When the status of the player changes, they may no longer be able to access the corresponding forums. The posts made by players while accessing the forums will stay even after they leave. They can be viewed by new players who get access later on. *My Faction (Contains threads related to the faction the player is currently part of.) *My Company (Contains threads related to the company the player is currently part of.) *Donator Forum (Exclusive for players with donator/subscriber status.) *VIP Corner (Exclusive for those with at least 1,000 positive karma.) *Christmas Town (Exclusive for players who made a Christmas town map.) *Wiki (Exclusive for Wiki contributors and editors.) *Reporter Panel (Exclusive for players who have Reporter status for Torn City Times Newspaper.) *Elimination Team forum during the [[Elimination]] competition in September. ===Main Forums=== These forums are accessible to all torn players at all times. Forum search parameters now include (can be combined for more precise results): * Plus (+text): Must contain text * Minus (-text): Must exclude text * by: player_name OR player_ID: Search all posts by a specific player * Wildcard (text*): Must contain words starting with text (wildcard only works on the right side) * Double quotes ("text"): Must contain the exact word or phrase * Pipe (text1 | text2): Must contain either text1 or text2, or both * Parenthesis (+"text1" +(text2 | text3)): Must have text1 AND text2 OR text3 Searches are limited to 2 characters or more and the following have been excluded from the search database to improve performance: an as at be by de en in is it la of on or to Search results will display relative timestamps, last edited and last replied information. ==Karma== A player's karma is a measurement of the likes and dislikes their forum posts have received. The lowest possible karma a player can have is zero, regardless of the number of dislikes their posts have received. Upon reaching a total of 1000 karma, players are given access to a special forum called "VIP Corner". A player will not receive/lose karma in the following scenarios: * The post is under thirty characters long * The thread is locked or in the graveyard * The thread is in your faction’s forum, company forum or elimination contest forum * The person liking/disliking the post is a new player, or has not posted in the forum in a long time * The person liking/disliking the post has been mass-rating a single user’s posts Do be aware that once you rate a post, you only have a short period of time to change your rating before it becomes permanent. ==See Also== * [[Messages]] * [[Chat]] * (Related Archived) [[IRC Chat]] == Historical Notes == * The Forum currently uses [[wikipedia:TinyMCE|TinyMCE]] * During the RESPO update the ‘Old Forums’ were archived, threads created before this update can still be viewed [https://www.torn.com/old_forums.php here]. == Patch History == {{Patch History|0}}</text>
